title: Hormuz Food & Energy Security Crisis Tracker Update — Mon Aug 31, 2026
summary: The US struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Aug 30 after detecting preparations to mine the Strait of Hormuz, ending a month of calm just two days after CENTCOM declared the strait 'cleared and open.' Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes on US-linked bases in Jordan and the UAE through Aug 31, with Jordan intercepting eight missiles and the UAE intercepting a drone near Al Minhad airbase. Oil markets reacted sharply, with Brent crude climbing from the high-$80s to $93.03/bbl, while global wheat futures pushed to $751.65/bushel, the highest since February 2023. The flare-up casts fresh doubt on the durability of the Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping corridor agreed just five days earlier.

title: Hormuz Food & Energy Security Crisis Tracker Update — Fri Aug 28, 2026
summary: Iran and Oman finalized a temporary 7-mile-wide shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 26, complete with a mine-clearing project and revenue-sharing deal, though Tehran insists the strait remains officially closed pending US sanctions relief. Brent crude fell 2.5% to $86.38/bbl on the news before steadying near $87.65-89.68/bbl on Aug 27 as hot US PCE inflation data offset de-escalation optimism. Tanker traffic has not recovered despite the deal — PortWatch and Vortexa data show just 2-3 transits/day, the lowest since early May. Separately, global wheat prices climbed to $734.30/bushel, the highest since June 2023 and +25% since January, as Black Sea tensions compound Gulf-driven cost pressures.
